question.problem:
Given the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],$ find row operations that transform $A$ into the $3\times 3$  identity matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Let's consider the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,{I}_{3}]$ where ${I}_{3}$ is the $3\times 3$ identity. Then, by applying the following row operations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,{I}_{3}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  \\  & =[{I}_{3}\,|\,{A}^{-1}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operations are ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3},$ while

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
